key_insight: Combining a Bayesian coordination layer with an adversarial multi-agent LLM setup within a low-code platform improves reliability and mitigates error propagation when automating scientific code workflows.
problem_solved: Addresses unreliable and cascading failures in multi-agent LLM pipelines for AI-for-Science tasks and the difficulty of evaluating solutions in domains with ill-defined success metrics, while making automation accessible via low-code interfaces.
method: Bayesian adversarial multi-agent coordination: three cooperating LLM agents (e.g., a Task Manager that structures user input, a Code/Execution agent, and a Critic/Verifier agent) exchange beliefs and updates under a Bayesian framework.

Low-code Platform (LCP) integration: orchestration layer exposes simple user primitives, iterative agent communication, and automated code generation/execution hooks to shorten the scientist-to-code loop.
Adversarial validation loop: the verifier/critic adversarially probes outputs, surfaces failure modes, and the Bayesian updater adjusts agent trust/confidence to reduce error propagation.
impact: Makes AI-driven scientific coding more robust, auditable, and usable by practitioners—reducing manual debugging and helping teams quantify uncertainty in domains where success is hard to define.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing three LLM agents (Task Manager → Code Agent → Critic) with Bayesian belief-update arrows between them

paper_title: AI-for-Science Low-code Platform with Bayesian Adversarial Multi-Agent Framework
paper_authors: Zihang Zeng, Jiaquan Zhang, Pengze Li, Yuan Qi, Xi Chen
